newsitem.title: JAPAN: Thai move to hurt fin sector credit outlook--S&P.
newsitem.headline: Thai move to hurt fin sector credit outlook--S&P.

text.p: The managed flotation of the Thai baht on Wednesday will have a negative impact on the credit outlook for the country's financial sector, an analyst with rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp said.

Peter Fikora, associate director of financial services at Standard & Poor's in Melbourne, told Reuters Financial Television in Tokyo that the immediate blow to the sector would be limited by the fact that firms' offshore liabilities are to some extent offset on their balance sheets, but there could be more fallout down the road.
"The immediate impact on the financial sector will obviously be negative because of the flow-through impact on asset quality," he said.

The Thai baht, which has been battered by speculative attacks, fell sharply on Wednesday after the Bank of Thailand announced it had let the currency float -- a de facto devaluation. The country's discount rate -- the rate at which the central bank lends to commercial banks -- was also raised to 12.5 percent from 10.5 percent.

"(The) concern for us is really what the devaluation impact will be on the quality of borrowing and this quite obviously will have a flow-through impact on the situation with individual banks," he said.
"A lot of borrowers often do take foreign currency loans on the basis that they have got cash flows that can match that but that's not always the case."

He added: "The important thing to watch for really is obviously the extent of the market devaluation because this will obviously determine the ultimate financial losses that they do need to take and certainly the second is the mismatched positions that the borrowers are maintaining."
Asked about the Thai government's response to financial market instability, Fikora said the government would have to carry out its initiatives strictly to restore market confidence in the government.
